slides.title: Buyers shouldn't need a meeting [to judge fit].
slides.lede: B2B website conversion improves when suitable buyers can answer questions about fit, fees and delivery, then take the right next step.

slides.title: Most B2B buyers [prefer to research alone]
slides.text: of 646 B2B buyers surveyed preferred a rep-free experience. That supports self-directed evaluation, not removing human help.

items.title: Do you handle firms like ours?
items.text: Approved examples showing sector, scale and scope.

items.title: Can we afford this?
items.text: Your charging model and real scope assumptions.

items.title: Who will deliver the work?
items.text: Named delivery roles and relevant experience.

items.title: Can I explain this internally?
items.text: A shareable summary with evidence links.

slides.title: "Who actually does the work?" [beats "trust"]
slides.text: Record the buyer's wording from recent proposals and lost opportunities. A specific question tells you what evidence to publish. A vague one could mean anything.

slides.title: The website and the seller [said different things]
slides.text: of B2B buyers reported inconsistencies between website information and what sellers told them.

cards.label: Enquiry
cards.text: A contact request associated with a service.

cards.label: Accepted opportunity
cards.text: A request the firm agrees is worth pursuing.
